newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CM Hai Hong in HK$3.86 bln share issue.
newsitem.headline: CM Hai Hong in HK$3.86 bln share issue.

text.p: China Merchants Hai Hong Holdings Co Ltd said on Wednesday it would raise HK$3.86 billion through an issue of new shares at HK$6.03 per share.
The funds raised would be used to acquire interests in toll roads and container businesses in China, the company said.

The company's parent, China Merchants Holdings, would subscribe for 650 million new shares, and has agreed to place 260 million existing shares it holds to the market, Hai Hong chairman Li Yinfei told a news conference.
"China Merchants Hai Hong will become the flagship of the China Merchants group in Hong Kong, and the group will continue to inject good quality infrastructure projects into Hai Hong," Li said.
China Merchants group is ultimately controlled by China's Communications Ministry.
Hai Hong will acquire 23.7 percent of Shenzhen-listed China International Marine Containers Ltd at HK$6.702 per B share, director Zhao Qingsheng told reporters.
The value of the assets to be acquired was HK$534 million, but the actual consideration to be paid was HK$320 million, he said.
The deal will be completed through the purchase of a company that holds the existing shares.
China Marine B shares ended at HK$11.40 on Wednesday.

Hai Hong will also acquire five toll roads in China, including roads in Guangdong, Guangxi and Zhejiang from its parent and from Union Bank of Hong Kong Ltd and China Merchants Direct Investments Ltd, both of which are members of the China Merchants group.
A Peregrine Investments executive said there was a good initial response to the placement of the existing Hai Hong shares in the market.
Further details of the share issue and placement as well as the acquisitions would be issued later, he said.
